𝐀𝐍𝐃 𝐓𝐇𝐀𝐓’𝐒 𝐓𝐇𝐀𝐓…⁣
⁣
This movie is Martin Scorsese’s most underrated picture. And I would argue it’s also his most ambitious. I think it might just be my third favorite Scorsese movie ever (after Taxi Driver and Goodfellas). Every time I watch it I fall in love all over again. ⁣
⁣
The way this movie captures the sheer mechanics of Las Vegas is breathtaking. The costumes alone were insane: Robert De Niro had seventy outfits, Sharon Stone had forty, and they both got to keep them. And it’s not just for show. Every detail, from the suits to the glittering casinos, serves the story. You can feel the desperation and obsession that defined Vegas during that era. ⁣
⁣
Speaking of obsession, the performances are off the charts. Joe Pesci takes his dynamic energy from Raging Bull (1980) to new heights. The chemistry between him and De Niro is electric. Most of their conversations were improvised: Scorsese would just tell them where to start and end, and the rest was pure genius. Then there’s Sharon Stone, who simply effervesces as the gold-digging, ruthless hustler Ginger. After seeing her performance, I can’t imagine anyone else playing her. She deserved far more recognition than the Academy gave her. And honestly, she makes Susan Sarandon’s win that year feel a little unjust.⁣
⁣
While Goodfellas (1990) gave us the ground-level view of blue-collar New York gangsters, 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐢𝐧𝐨 (𝟏𝟗𝟗𝟓) shows the ones who run the whole show: the guys controlling the flow of money, the power, the lust, and the inevitable fall. It’s the most uncompromising studio picture of the 1990s. A masterclass in direction, performance, and storytelling. It’s not just a Scorsese film. It transcends him.

source_details.synopsis: Casino is a 1995 epic gangster film directed by Martin Scorsese and adapted by Scorsese and Nicholas Pileggi from the latter's nonfiction book Casino: Love and Honor in Las Vegas. It stars Robert De Niro, Sharon Stone, Joe Pesci, Don Rickles, Kevin Pollak, Frank Vincent and James Woods. The film was the eighth collaboration between director Scorsese and De Niro. Casino follows Sam "Ace" Rothstein (De Niro), a gambling expert handicapper who is asked by the Chicago Outfit to oversee the day-to-day casino and hotel operations at the Tangiers Casino in Las Vegas.
